abstract: Background: PDAC is a highly aggressive malignancy driven predominantly by activating KRAS mutations, and allele-specific and pan-RAS inhibitors have emerged as candidate targeted therapies. Evidence supporting them is dominated by experimental studies of which the models differ widely in how faithfully they reproduce human disease, and clinical maturity is uneven across alleles. Objectives: The objective of this study was to evaluate allele-stratified RAS-inhibitor activity across KRAS subtypes in PDAC, synthesizing experimental and clinical evidence separately, and determine whether the principal conclusions of the review survive when the experimental evidence is stratified by the level of model validation achieved. Methods: PubMed, Cochrane Library, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched from inception to 26 June 2026, with a pre-specified updated search in June 2026. Experimental studies were appraised with a modified JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Quasi-Experimental Studies supplemented by preclinical-specific reporting domains, and were independently classified by the highest level of model validation achieved, from conventional two-dimensional cell lines through to multi-model validation spanning patient-derived and immunocompetent in vivo systems; clinical studies were appraised with ROBINS-I. Experimental and clinical evidence was synthesized separately. Single-arm proportions from KRAS G12C trials were pooled on the logit scale using inverse-variance random-effects meta-analysis with Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals, and certainty was rated using GRADE. Results: Twenty-four studies were included (twenty experimental and four early-phase, single-arm clinical trials). Four of the twenty experimental studies (20%) rested on conventional two-dimensional cell lines alone, nine (45%) incorporated patient-derived material, seven (35%) used immunocompetent models, and fourteen (70%) reproduced their principal finding in at least two independent model classes. The allele-dependent pattern of single-agent activity persisted when cell-line-only studies were set aside, whereas 6 of the 17 studies reporting combination strategies provided no confirmation in any higher-order system. Across three single-arm KRAS G12C trials, the pooled objective response rate was 36.9% (95% CI, 9.8-75.7%; I2 = 66.2%; individual trials 21.1%, 45.5%, and 46.9%), the pooled disease control rate was 85.9% (95% CI, 62.1-95.8%; I2 = 0%; individual datasets 81.8%, 84.2%, and 93.8%), and the grade ≥ 3 treatment-related adverse event rate was 23.8% (95% CI, 11.2-43.5%; I2 = 0%). GRADE certainty was very low for all three outcomes. Conclusions: The available evidence is consistent with allele-dependent activity of RAS-targeted therapy in PDAC and supports biomarker-guided treatment selection, but the clinical evidence base is confined to small, single-arm, early-phase trials of KRAS G12C inhibitors. The pooled estimates are exploratory descriptions of observed activity in selected early-phase populations, not comparative estimates of treatment efficacy. KRAS G12D-directed therapy remains at a substantially earlier stage of clinical validation than KRAS G12C-directed therapy despite a much larger preclinical literature.
key_points_ko: KRAS G12C 억제제 단일군 임상시험 3건의 통합 객관적 반응률(ORR)은 36.9%(95% CI, 9.8-75.7%)였습니다.
통합 질병 조절률(DCR)은 85.9%(95% CI, 62.1-95.8%), 3등급 이상의 중대한 치료 관련 부작용 발생률은 23.8%였습니다.
KRAS G12D 표적 치료는 전임상 연구 규모가 큼에도 불구하고 임상적 검증 단계는 G12C보다 현저히 초기 수준에 머물러 있습니다.
summary_ko: 췌장관선암(PDAC) 환자를 대상으로 KRAS 변이 유형별 RAS 억제제의 효과를 확인하기 위해 24건의 연구(전임상 20건, 초기 단일군 임상시험 4건)를 종합 분석했습니다. KRAS G12C 억제제 관련 3건의 단일군 임상시험을 메타분석한 결과, 객관적 반응률(ORR)은 36.9%, 질병 조절률(DCR)은 85.9%로 집계되었습니다. 3등급 이상의 치료 관련 이상반응 발생률은 23.8%였으며 전반적인 근거 수준(GRADE)은 매우 낮음으로 평가되었습니다. 연구진은 대립유전자별 표적 치료의 가능성을 지지하면서도, KRAS G12D 표적 치료의 임상 검증은 G12C에 비해 아직 매우 초기 단계라고 결론지었습니다.
title: Allele-Stratified Activity of RAS Inhibitors in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma: A Systematic Review and Exploratory Meta-Analysis
